subject.title: Feature: HMAC/token-based mutual auth for inter-agent sessions_send

question: What sender-authentication contract should OpenClaw support for inter-session `sessions_send` messages?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but the safe fix depends on maintainer intent for key ownership, replay semantics, allowed-sender policy, fail-closed defaults, config shape, and interaction with scoped Gateway tokens and plugin-based identity workarounds.

options.title: Design core sender-auth contract
options.body: Create a narrow security design for `sessions_send` sender proof, replay protection, key lifecycle, migration/default behavior, and tests before any implementation PR.

options.title: Prefer plugin/envelope hooks first
options.body: Keep core behavior unchanged for now and only add or document a pre-receive/plugin hook path for ClawHub identity envelopes such as IdentyClaw.

options.title: Defer to broader federation/scoped-token work
options.body: Leave this issue open as blocked until the related Gateway token-scope and cross-gateway identity decisions settle.

recommendation.title: Design core sender-auth contract
recommendation.body: Create a narrow security design for `sessions_send` sender proof, replay protection, key lifecycle, migration/default behavior, and tests before any implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal is his work on inter-session provenance and session-tool security scoping around the affected path.
